explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/903: for n = p² + p + 1 with p a prime power and A_1, …, A_t ⊆ {1,…,n} with every pair contained in exactly one A_i, is it true that t > n implies t ≥ n + p? (proved by Erdős–Fowler–Sós–Wilson). The Lean statement: for every prime power p and every H ⊆ 𝒫(Fin (p²+p+1)) that is a pairwise balanced design (blocks of size ≥ 2, each 2-set in exactly one block), p²+p+1 < |H| implies p²+p+1+p ≤ |H|. Requiring blocks of size ≥ 2 is standard and harmless (singleton or empty blocks never cover pairs), using a Finset of blocks rules out repeated blocks (which the uniqueness condition excludes anyway), and the degenerate design with the whole ground set as a block has t = 1 and is irrelevant under t > n. Faithful.
